**Runs Temporal 1 · macOS and Linux** · [registry page ↗](https://doze-dev.com/registry/doze/temporal/)

<!-- recipe:start -->

Run a Temporal server for your workflows and workers, with its Web UI and the
namespaces you declare.

This is Temporal's own dev server, from the Temporal CLI: one binary with the
Temporal services, a SQLite store and the Web UI. No JVM, no Docker, no
database to set up.

## A server

```hcl
module temporal "flows" {
  version = "1.1"
  port    = 7233
  ui_port = 8233

  namespace "orders" {}
}
```

Declare `port`: it gives the server its address, which `doze url` prints and
an app references.

```sh
doze url flows
# flows.shop.doze:7233
```

```hcl
app "worker" {
  run = "go run ./cmd/worker"
  env = { TEMPORAL_ADDRESS = module.flows.address }
}
```

The Web UI listens on `ui_port`; `headless = true` turns it off.

## It stays up

Temporal does not sleep. doze runs the server itself rather than waking it on
a connection, and workers long-poll it all the time anyway, so it runs while
the stack is up. A `sleep` duration on it is an error (`sleep = "never"` is allowed and changes nothing). See
[Sleep and wake](/hcl/sleep/).

<!-- recipe:end -->

## Reference

A local Temporal dev server: a single pure-Go binary bundling the Temporal services, a SQLite store, and the Web UI, with no JVM or Docker. Supervised and always-on (workers long-poll it); connect via TEMPORAL_ADDRESS.

### Every field at once

<!-- ground:skip -->
```hcl
module temporal "dev" {
  version = "1.1"
  port    = 7233
  ui_port = 8233

  namespace "orders"  {}
  namespace "billing" {}
}
```

### Versions you can declare

The `version =` you write is the engine's own version. Declare a series and
doze pins its newest published build, or declare an exact build. Either way it
is fetched, verified and pinned in `doze.lock`, so it never moves on its own.

| `version =` | pins (today) | exact builds |
|---|---|---|
| `1.0` | `1.0.0` | 1 |
| `1.1` | `1.1.2` | 3 |
| `1.2` | `1.2.0` | 1 |
| `1.3` | `1.3.0` | 1 |
| `1.4` | `1.4.1` | 2 |
| `1.5` | `1.5.1` | 2 |
| `1.6` | `1.6.2` | 3 |
| `1.7` | `1.7.3` | 4 |
| `1.8` | `1.8.2` | 3 |

### Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | — | temporal CLI version **Required.** |
| `port` | number | `7233` | frontend gRPC port |
| `ui_port` | number | `8233` | Web UI port |
| `headless` | bool | `false` | disable the Web UI |

Every module block also takes doze's own fields: `port`, `listen`, `sleep`,
`after`, `enabled`, `routes`, `count` and `for_each`
([doze.hcl reference](/reference/doze-hcl/)).

### Nested blocks

**`namespace "<name>" { … }`** — a namespace to create (repeatable; label = name; retention, description)

_The module does not list this block's fields yet._

**`restart { … }`** — supervisor restart policy (policy, backoff, max_retries)

### Module releases

The releases of the module that provide this engine. doze picks the newest
one that fits your doze and your `version =`, and pins it in `doze.lock`;
you never write these. Older releases stay available for pinned lockfiles.
